paper.title: Distributed algorithms for learning and cognitive medium access with logarithmic regret

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed learning and access with known number of secondary users
unmapped: N = U secondary users (players), K = C channels with U <= C; each user senses one channel per slot, collision if two users choose same channel; no communication among users
number of users U is known to every user
regret is system (sum) regret vs. orthogonal allocation to U best channels
all channel means distinct and in (0,1)
settings.definition_quote: In each channel $i$ and slot $k$, the primary user transmits i.i.d. with probability $1-\mu_i>0$... We assume the collision model under which if two or more users transmit in the same channel then none of the transmissions go through.

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed learning and access under unknown number of users
unmapped: N = U players unknown but fixed, U <= C = K channels; collision model, no communication
users estimate U from collision feedback
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider the scenario, where the number of users $U$ is unknown (but fixed throughout the duration of transmissions and $U\leq C$, the number of channels).

settings.name_in_paper: Centralized learning and access for multiple users (multiple plays)
unmapped: central agent selects m = U distinct channels out of K = C each slot (multiple plays)
settings.definition_quote: We now consider multiple secondary users under centralized access policies where there is joint learning and access by a central agent on behalf of all the $U$ users.

algorithms.name: rho^EST (random allocation with estimation of number of users)
Centralized learning policy rho^CENT with g^MEAN

symbols.sum_top_U: sum over the U best channels m*
symbols.sum_U_worst: sum over the U-worst channels i

source.label: thm:lowerbnd_cent
source.quote: The scheme in Algorithm~\ref{algo:cent} based on the $g^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}}$ satisfies for any $n>0$, R(n;\mubf,U, \cent(\statbf^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}}))\leq \sum_{m =1}^U \sum_{i\in U\mbox{-worst}} \sum_{k=1}^U \frac{\Delta(m^*,i) }{U}\left[\frac{ 8 \log n}{\Delta(m^*,i)^2} + 1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\right].

results.notes: Theorem framed as a recap of Anantharam et al., but the g^MEAN bound is proved in the appendix by extending Auer et al. The inner sum over k with 1/U cancels. The other parts (lower bound, g^OPT optimality) are recorded as cited results.

symbols.Delta_ik: gap between U-worst channel i and k-th best channel

source.label: lemma:uworstrandalloc
source.quote: Under the $\randalloc$ scheme in Algorithm~\ref{algo:randalloc}, the total time spent by any user $j=1,\ldots, U$, in any $i\in U$-worst channel is given by \Ebb[T_{i,j}(n)] \leq \sum_{k=1}^U\Bigl[\frac{ 8 \log n}{\Delta(i,k^*)^2} + 1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big].

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a U-worst channel by a single user.

symbols.sum_pairs: sum over a = 1..U and b = a+1..C

source.label: lemma:numintfrandalloc
source.quote: Under the $\randalloc$ scheme in Algorithm~\ref{algo:randalloc}, \Ebb[T'(n;\randalloc)] \leq U\sum_{a=1}^U \sum_{b=a+1}^C \left[ \frac{8 \log n}{\Delta(a^*,b^*)^2}+\!1\! + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\right]

results.notes: Bounds expected number of slots with wrong top-U rank estimates. N = U users. Lemma (lemma:Tdashdash) states the same bound for rho^EST.

source.label: thm:intfrandalloc
source.quote: The expected number of collisions in the $U$-best channels under $\randalloc(U,C, \bfg^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}} )$ scheme satisfies \Ebb[M(n)] \leq U(\Ebb[\Upsilon(U,U)]+1)\,\Ebb[T'_j(n)]. Hence, from \eqref{eqn:tij_randalloc}, \eqref{eqn:tdashj} and \eqref{eqn:Pi}, $M(n) = O(\log n)$.

results.notes: Expected number of collisions in U-best channels; E[Upsilon(U,U)] <= binom(2U-1,U)-1 by Lemma (lemma:Pi).

source.label: thm:randalloc
source.quote: The policy $\randalloc(U,C,\bfg^{\mbox{\tiny MEAN}} )$ in Algorithm~\ref{algo:randalloc} has $\Theta(\log n)$ regret.

results.notes: System regret against orthogonal allocation to the U best channels, defined via expected successful transmissions (means), hence pseudo-regret. Explicit constant obtainable by combining Prop. (prop:bounds) upper bound with Lemmas; exponential in U via binom(2U-1,U).

conditions: regret conditioned on the event that no user over-estimates U

source.label: lemma:cond_regret
source.quote: When all the $U$ secondary users implement $\unknownalloc$ policy, ... \Ebb[M(n)|\Cc(n;U)]\leq U \sum_{k=1}^U \xi(n;k) \leq U^2 \xi^*(n;U). From \eqref{eqn:regret_Mbnd}, we have $R(n)|\Cc(n;U)$ is $ O( \max(\xi^*(n;U), \log n))$ for any $n\in \Nbb$.

results.notes: Conditional regret; stated as O(max(xi*, log n)); expression written as a sum for parseability with explicit U^2 factor from collision bound. Also bounds conditional U-worst pulls by same expression as Lemma (lemma:uworstrandalloc).

tuning: xi(n;1)=1, xi(n;k) = omega(log n) for k>1

source.quote: With threshold functions $\xi$ satisfying conditions in \eqref{eqn:cond_xi}, the policy $\unknownalloc(n,C,\statbf_j(m), \xi)$ in Algorithm~\ref{algo:unknownalloc} satisfies \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n;\mubf, U, \unknownalloc)}{\xi^*(n;U)} <\infty.

results.notes: Implies O(f(n) log n) regret for any f(n) -> infinity. Horizon n is an input to the algorithm (doubling extension mentioned in footnote).
